terlingua.github.io has the concept of "books". what if these books and the associated multiple choice questions could be made into a native Android App? how would it work? what programming languages, frameworks, and concepts would we use to make it the best future proof native Android app possible that works from github actions and obtainium without google play? fully self contained no Internet access needed but can share progress using either local transfer or over messaging apps or email or whatever?
it should use the latest stable version of everything including all dependencies and github actions 
however, we should allow the app to be installed on older versions of Android as well 
the book files will stay in the same format and during build time we will somehow include all this information in the apk itself 
we will have optional sound as well as haptic feedback where the device allows 
use kotlin, kotlin compose, and all the modern technology
the github dot com repository will be public at https://github.com/terlingua/terlingua-android/
I have already added these four secrets and the names I hope are self explanatory 
KEYSTORE_BASE64
KEYSTORE_PASSWORD
KEY_ALIAS
KEY_PASSWORD
every single push should build a new FULL release APK, not a pre-release ONLY for Android 
it is ok to create a single big APK that servers multiple platforms (within github dot com limits)
the goal here is native performance 
on device persistent local storage
and useful across all devices -- candy bar phones, foldable phones, tablets, and possibly even notebook style PCs that support Android APK installs
